prose_findings.claim: sampled reads cover 23 of 35 controller update_ids
prose_findings.assessment: The prediction receipts cover 16 distinct update IDs. The 23-ID union includes plans-only reads, which do not supply one-step prediction comparisons. The structured queried status is valid, but this prose overstates prediction coverage.

prose_findings.claim: sampled selection fields carry inconsistent index/update_id labels
prose_findings.assessment: No such source inconsistency is established. Array offsets index the selected result rows; update_id identifies the original controller update. For example updates/7 in result 9f82e96df515e538083f467ac77bd5d52fffcaf73b1486b9a03aa34f98f8088f is update_id 34 with selected iteration 31. Treating these different indices as inconsistent unnecessarily discounts valid evidence.

Synchronous scheduling excludes automatic injection of computation time as physical feedback delay. The ruled_out label should be limited to that mechanism; computational budgets can still influence selected plans. No general causal exclusion of all computation-related effects is supported.

Eleven facts and 74 selectors exceed the requested usual 2-4 key facts; the limitations array is empty although limitations appear in attribution and recommendations. Citation volume is not treated as a quality score.

positive_findings: Terminal reach, sampled settling and computation are explicitly distinguished.
No numerical check, backend execution, physical change, or task improvement is claimed.
Raw objective weights are not used to establish cost-term importance, and one-step comparisons are not treated as complete causal identification.
